{{Short description|American physicist}}

'''Tom Tombrello''' (1936–2014) was Robert H. Goddard Professor of Physics at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. He earned B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. degrees in physics, all at [[Rice University]].  He studied nuclear reactions in the 1960s, which helped show how chemical elements are created.<ref name="MyUser_M.caltech.edu_September_14_2015c">{{cite web |author= |date= 14 October 2014|title=Remembering Tom Tombrello |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/remembering-tom-tombrello-44037 |accessdate=September 14, 2015 |newspaper=caltech.edu}}</ref>

Tombrello chaired the Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy at Caltech from 1998 to 2008. He helped create Physics 11, a freshman physics course and research fellowship that required students to audition by solving a pair of challenging toy research problems called "hurdles". On May 30, 1997, Tombrello received an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] from the Faculty of Science and Technology at [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/|title = Honorary doctorates - Uppsala University, Sweden | date=9 June 2023 }}</ref> In 2010, Tombrello became a founding trustee of the [[London Institute for Mathematical Sciences]].
